title: Determinant vanishes without a perfect matching
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $A$ be an $n\times n$ Boolean matrix. If the bipartite graph with one copy of the indices on each side and an edge from $i$ on the left to $j$ on the right exactly when $A_{i,j}=\mathrm{true}$ has no perfect matching, then the determinant of the polynomial matrix with entry $X_{i,j}$ at such edges and zero elsewhere is zero.
hypotheses_covered: The associated bipartite graph has no perfect matching
